questions.question: Allah Rakha, Sabir Khan, Pandit Kishan Maharaj, Pandit Gyan Prakash Ghosh and Sandip Das are famous players of which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Tabla**__.

__
 
• The **Tabla** is a widely popular percussion instrument in Indian classical music, consisting of two drums – the **Dayan** (right drum) and the **Bayan** (left drum).
 
• **Allah Rakha** and **Sabir Khan** were renowned tabla maestros known for their contributions to Indian classical music and fusion performances.
 
• **Pandit Kishan Maharaj** and **Pandit Gyan Prakash Ghosh** were also celebrated tabla players whose expertise elevated the instrument’s prominence in Hindustani classical music.
 
• **Sandip Das** is another well-known tabla artist who specializes in Indian classical music and has collaborated in global fusion music projects.
 
• The **Tabla** is used in various forms of music, including **Hindustani classical, devotional, film music, and fusion genres.**
 
• The instrument is known for its **versatility**, capable of producing intricate rhythms and dynamic tones that enhance musical compositions.
 
• The **Tabla** has two primary components: the smaller, higher-pitched drum (**Dayan**) made of wood, and the larger, bass-pitched drum (**Bayan**), often made of metal or clay.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

 __
 
• The **Mridangam** is a percussion instrument primarily used in **Carnatic classical music**.
 
• It is a barrel-shaped drum with two heads, producing a rich and resonant tone.
 
• The Mridangam is considered the **primary rhythmic accompaniment** in Carnatic concerts.
 
• It is made from **jackfruit wood** and is played using both hands.
 
• Famous Mridangam players include **Palghat Mani Iyer** and **Umayalpuram K. Sivaraman**.
 
 
 
• **Pakhavaj**__
 __
 
• The **Pakhavaj** is a traditional Indian drum used in **Dhrupad music**, a genre of Hindustani classical music.
 
• It is a cylindrical drum with two heads, and its playing technique is similar to the Mridangam.
 
• The Pakhavaj has a **deep, resonant sound** and is considered the precursor to the tabla.
 
• It is commonly used in **devotional and classical music.**

• It is a pot-like instrument played with fingers, palms, and sometimes knuckles.
 
• The Ghatam produces a **unique metallic tone** and is known for its rhythmic versatility.
 
• Famous Ghatam players include **T.H. Vikku Vinayakram** and **S. Karthick**.

questions.question: Which method of national income accounting involves classifying production centres into primary, secondary and tertiary sectors?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Production Approach**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Production Approach** is one of the three main methods used in **national income accounting** to calculate a country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
 
• It involves classifying **production centres** into three major sectors: **primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors**.
 
• **Primary Sector:** This includes activities related to the extraction and harvesting of natural resources such as **agriculture, forestry, fishing, and mining.**
 
• **Secondary Sector:** This includes industrial activities that involve the **manufacturing and processing** of goods, such as factories and construction industries.
 
• **Tertiary Sector:** This includes services like **banking, education, healthcare, trade, and transport.**
 
• The approach calculates GDP by summing up the **value added** at each stage of production across all sectors.
 
• The method avoids the issue of **double counting** by focusing on the value added at each production stage rather than the total value of sales.
 
• It provides a clear picture of the **contribution of different sectors** to the economy, which helps policymakers in planning and resource allocation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Residual Approach**__

 __
 
• The **Residual Approach** is not a standard method of calculating national income. However, it is sometimes used in **specific cases** to calculate the income of certain sectors when direct measurement is not possible.
 
• This method relies on **indirect estimation** by subtracting known components from the total to derive the unknown component.
 
 
 
• **Income Approach**__
 __
 
• The **Income Approach** calculates GDP by summing up all **incomes earned** by individuals and businesses, including wages, rents, interests, and profits.
 
• This method focuses on the **distribution side** of the economy rather than the production side.
 
 
 
• **Expenditure Approach**__
 
 
• The **Expenditure Approach** calculates GDP by summing up all **spending** on final goods and services in the economy, including consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports.
 
• This method is useful for analyzing the **demand side** of the economy.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about cell is correct?

options.text: Powerhouse of a cell is plastid.
Cell is a functional unit of life.
Cell membrane of a cell is hard and rigid.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Cell is a functional unit of life.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **cell** is the **basic structural, functional, and biological unit of all living organisms**. It is often referred to as the **building block of life**.
 
• All living organisms, from the smallest bacteria to the largest plants and animals, are composed of one or more cells, making it the **functional unit of life**.
 
• Cells carry out essential processes such as **metabolism, growth, reproduction, and energy transformation**.
 
• The cell theory, proposed by **Schleiden and Schwann**, states that all living organisms are made of cells and that the cell is the fundamental unit of structure and function in all organisms.
 
• The cell contains various organelles such as the **nucleus, mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, and ribosomes**, which perform specialized functions to sustain life.
 
• Cells are classified into two types: **prokaryotic cells** (e.g., bacterial cells) and **eukaryotic cells** (e.g., plant and animal cells).
 
• This fundamental characteristic of cells makes them the **functional unit of life**, as they are responsible for carrying out all life processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bacterial cell contains cellulose.**__

 __
 
• Bacterial cells do not contain **cellulose**. Instead, their cell walls are made up of **peptidoglycan**, a polymer consisting of sugars and amino acids.
 
• Cellulose is a major component of the cell walls of **plants**, not bacteria.
 
 
 
• **Powerhouse of a cell is plastid.**__
 __
 
• The powerhouse of the cell is the **mitochondria**, not plastid. Mitochondria generate **ATP**, the energy currency of the cell.
 
• **Plastids**, such as chloroplasts, are involved in **photosynthesis** and other functions in plant cells but are not responsible for energy production.
 
 
 
• **Cell membrane of a cell is hard and rigid.**__
 
 
• The **cell membrane** is a **flexible and semi-permeable structure** made of a phospholipid bilayer. It is not hard and rigid.
 
• It controls the movement of substances in and out of the cell and provides structural support to the cell.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of double displacement reaction?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Na₂SO₄(aq) + BaCl₂(aq) → BaSO₄(s) + 2NaCl(aq)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **double displacement reaction** occurs when two compounds exchange ions or elements to form two new compounds.
 
• In the reaction **Na₂SO₄(aq) + BaCl₂(aq) → BaSO₄(s) + 2NaCl(aq)**, there is an exchange of ions between **sodium sulfate (Na₂SO₄)** and **barium chloride (BaCl₂)**.
 
• The barium ions (Ba²⁺) react with sulfate ions (SO₄²−) to form an insoluble precipitate of **barium sulfate (BaSO₄)**, which is a characteristic of double displacement reactions.
 
• The sodium ions (Na⁺) and chloride ions (Cl−) form **sodium chloride (NaCl)**, which remains dissolved in the aqueous solution.
 
• This reaction demonstrates the concept of **precipitation**, where one of the products (BaSO₄) is insoluble and forms a solid in the solution.
 
• Double displacement reactions are commonly used in qualitative analysis and occur in aqueous solutions.
 
• This reaction is also a classic example of how **ionic compounds** interact in water to produce new compounds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **2Pb(NO₃)₂(s) + Heat → 2PbO(s) + 4NO₂(g) + O₂(g)**__

 __
 
• This is an example of a **decomposition reaction**, where a single compound breaks down into multiple simpler substances.
 
• Lead nitrate decomposes upon heating to form lead oxide, nitrogen dioxide gas, and oxygen gas.
 
• Decomposition reactions are often triggered by heat, light, or electricity.
 
 
 
• **ZnO + C → Zn + CO**__
 __
 
• This is a **reduction reaction**, where zinc oxide is reduced to zinc metal by carbon.
 
• Carbon acts as a reducing agent, converting zinc oxide into metallic zinc while itself getting oxidized to carbon monoxide.
 
• Such reactions are frequently seen in metallurgical processes for extracting metals from their ores.
 
 
 
• **Fe(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → FeSO₄(aq) + Cu(s)**__
 
 
• This is an example of a **single displacement reaction**, where iron displaces copper from copper sulfate to form iron sulfate and copper metal.
 
• Single displacement reactions typically occur when a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its compound.
 
• In this case, iron is more reactive than copper, which drives the reaction forward.

questions.question: Which part of our body is responsible for digestion?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Gastric glands**__.

__
 
• **Gastric glands** are located in the walls of the stomach and play a significant role in the process of **digestion**.
 
• They secrete **gastric juice**, which contains several important substances such as **hydrochloric acid (HCl), pepsinogen**, and **mucus**.
 
• **Hydrochloric acid** creates an acidic environment in the stomach, which is crucial for activating the enzyme **pepsin.**
 
• **Pepsin**, an enzyme secreted by the gastric glands, breaks down **proteins** into smaller peptides.
 
• **Mucus** protects the inner lining of the stomach from the corrosive effects of hydrochloric acid.
 
• The secretion of gastric juice is regulated by hormones such as **gastrin** and neural signals to ensure proper digestion.
 
• The gastric glands are a part of the **digestive system**, which works together with other organs to break down food and absorb nutrients.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kidney**__

 __
 
• The **kidneys** are vital organs responsible for **filtering blood**, removing waste products, and balancing electrolytes and fluids in the body.
 
• They are part of the **excretory system** and play no direct role in digestion.
 
• The kidneys also regulate **blood pressure** and produce hormones such as **erythropoietin** for red blood cell production.
 
 
 
• **Hands**__
 __
 
• **Hands** are primarily involved in performing tasks and physical activities, such as holding or preparing food, but they do not participate in the physiological process of digestion.
 
• They are part of the **musculoskeletal system**, which aids in movement and coordination.
 
 
 
• **Heart**__
 
 
• The **heart** is a muscular organ responsible for **pumping blood** throughout the body via the circulatory system.
 
• It does not have any function related to digestion but ensures that oxygen and nutrients are delivered to digestive organs.
 
• The heart is vital for maintaining **cardiovascular health** and overall body function.

questions.question: Which of the following is the darkest, or least reflective object in the Solar System with an albedo of 0.03?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1P/Halley**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **1P/Halley**, commonly known as **Halley's Comet**, is one of the most famous comets in the Solar System.
 
• It has an **albedo of 0.03**, which makes it one of the **darkest and least reflective objects** in the Solar System.
 
• An albedo of 0.03 means that Halley's Comet reflects only **3% of the sunlight** that falls on it, absorbing the rest.
 
• The comet is composed of **dark organic compounds** mixed with other elements like silicates and water ice, which contribute to its low reflectivity.
 
• Halley's Comet is a **periodic comet** and is visible from Earth approximately every **75-76 years**. Its last appearance was in **1986**, and it is expected to return in **2061**.
 
• It was named after **Edmond Halley**, who successfully predicted its periodic return after studying historical records of comet appearances.
 
• Because of its dark surface and unique characteristics, Halley's Comet provides significant insights into the composition and behavior of comets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **9P/Tempel 1**__

 __
 
• **9P/Tempel 1** is another periodic comet in the Solar System.
 
• It was the target of the **Deep Impact mission** conducted by NASA in 2005, which studied its composition by colliding a spacecraft probe with its surface.
 
• This comet has a higher albedo than Halley's Comet and reflects more sunlight.
 
 
 
• **2P/Encke**__
 __
 
• **2P/Encke** is known for having the **shortest orbital period** of any known comet, completing a trip around the Sun approximately every **3.3 years**.
 
• Its albedo is higher than Halley's Comet, making it more reflective.
 
 
 
• **19P/Borrelly**__
 
 
• **19P/Borrelly** is another periodic comet that has been studied closely by spacecraft.
 
• It was visited by NASA's **Deep Space 1 mission** in 2001, which provided detailed images of its nucleus.
 
• Its albedo is slightly higher than Halley's Comet, but it is still relatively dark compared to other celestial bodies.

questions.question: The voting age was reduced from 21 years to 18 years by the ________ Constitutional Amendment Act of 1988.

• The **61st Constitutional Amendment Act of 1988** lowered the **voting age** from **21 years** to **18 years** for elections to the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies.
 
• This amendment was introduced to encourage greater **youth participation** in the electoral process and strengthen democracy.
 
• The change was made by amending **Article 326** of the Indian Constitution, which governs elections to the Lok Sabha and state assemblies.
 
• The amendment recognized the **importance of youth** in shaping the nation's future and gave them the right to vote at an earlier age.
 
• The reduction in voting age aimed to empower the younger generation and ensure their **voices and opinions** are represented in the political process.
 
• This decision was a landmark in the democratic history of India as it expanded the electorate significantly, adding millions of new voters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **51st Constitutional Amendment Act**__

 __
 
• The **51st Constitutional Amendment Act** of 1984 provided for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes in Meghalaya, Nagaland, and Mizoram in the Lok Sabha.
 
• This amendment aimed to protect the **interests of Scheduled Tribes** in these states.
 
• It is unrelated to the reduction of the voting age.
 
 
 
• **71st Constitutional Amendment Act**__
 __
 
• The **71st Constitutional Amendment Act** of 1992 added **Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali** to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, making them official languages of India.
 
• This amendment dealt with **linguistic diversity** rather than voting rights.
 
 
 
• **41st Constitutional Amendment Act**__
 
 
• The **41st Constitutional Amendment Act** of 1976 extended the term of office for members of Parliament and state legislatures during emergencies.
 
• This amendment was passed to address political stability during times of national crisis.
 
• It does not relate to voting age changes.

questions.question: Which of the following pair is incorrect?

options.text: Fourth Five Year Plan - Poverty Removal Goal
First Five Year Plan - Agricultural Development
Second Five Year Plan - Nehru Mahalanobis Model

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Fourth Five Year Plan - Poverty Removal Goal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fourth Five Year Plan** (1969–1974) primarily focused on **growth with stability** and emphasized **self-reliance** in agriculture and industrial production.
 
• Although the issue of **poverty** was recognized, the explicit goal of **poverty removal** was not the focus of this plan.
 
• The **poverty alleviation programs**, such as the **Garibi Hatao** initiative, were formally introduced during the **Fifth Five Year Plan** under the leadership of **Indira Gandhi**.
 
• The Fourth Plan also dealt with challenges such as the **Bangladesh Liberation War**, a severe drought, and the **oil crisis**, which impacted its outcomes.
 
• The Plan aimed at achieving **4.4% growth**, but the actual growth rate remained around **3.3%** due to economic and geopolitical challenges.
 
• Key features of this plan included the **Green Revolution**, which increased agricultural productivity, and the focus on reducing dependence on foreign aid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **First Five Year Plan - Agricultural Development**__

 __
 
• The **First Five Year Plan** (1951–1956) focused on the **agricultural sector**, recognizing its importance in the Indian economy.
 
• Major initiatives included the **Community Development Program** and investments in **irrigation projects** like the **Bhakra-Nangal Dam**.
 
• It was based on the **Harrod-Domar Model** for economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Second Five Year Plan - Nehru Mahalanobis Model**__
 __
 
• The **Second Five Year Plan** (1956–1961) was based on the **Mahalanobis Model**, which emphasized rapid **industrialization**, particularly in the capital goods sector.
 
• This plan laid the foundation for **public sector undertakings (PSUs)** like the **Bhilai Steel Plant** and **Durgapur Steel Plant**.
 
• It focused on achieving a **socialist pattern of society** as envisioned by **Jawaharlal Nehru**.

__
 
• **Privatization** refers to the process of transferring ownership, management, or control of government-owned enterprises or assets to private entities.
 
• **Disinvestment**__ involves the sale or liquidation of the government’s stake in public sector enterprises. It reduces government ownership and encourages private participation, thus promoting privatization.
 
• __**Outsourcing**__ is the practice of contracting out services or functions to private companies. This allows private firms to handle specific tasks or operations, fostering privatization in service delivery and operations.
 
• __**Urbanization**__ is a demographic process involving the migration of people from rural to urban areas and the expansion of urban centers. It does not directly promote privatization.
 
• Since both **Disinvestment** and **Outsourcing** are mechanisms that encourage privatization, the correct answer is **Only A and B**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 __
 
• **Definition:** The government reduces its stake in public enterprises by selling shares to private entities or the general public.
 
• **Purpose:** To generate revenue, improve efficiency, and reduce the fiscal burden on the government.
 
• **Examples:** Sale of government stakes in companies like Air India or BPCL.
 
 
 
• **Outsourcing**__
 __
 
• **Definition:** A process where businesses or governments contract private entities to perform certain tasks or services.
 
• **Applications:** IT services, customer support, cleaning, security, and transportation.
 
• **Examples:** Outsourcing ticketing services to private companies by Indian Railways.
 
 
 
• **Urbanization**__
 
 
• **Definition:** The process of people moving to urban areas, leading to the growth of cities.
 
• **Impact:** Urbanization impacts society, economy, and infrastructure but does not directly relate to privatization.
 
• **Examples:** Expansion of cities like Mumbai, Delhi, and Bengaluru.

• The **Government of India Act, 1935** laid the foundation for the federal structure in India.
 
• It introduced the concept of a **Federal Plan**, dividing powers between the **Central Government** and the **Provincial Governments**.
 
• The Act provided for three lists of subjects: the **Federal List**, the **Provincial List**, and the **Concurrent List**, which were later incorporated into the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• The Federal Plan established the principle of division of powers, which is now a key feature of India's **Constitutional framework.**
 
• The Act also introduced the system of **autonomy for provinces**, marking the beginning of decentralization in governance.
 
• This federal structure continues to be a significant feature of the **Constitution of India**, as seen in Articles related to the division of powers and responsibilities between the **Union and the States**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __

• **Joint Sitting of the Two Houses of Parliament**__
 __
 
• The concept of a **Joint Sitting** is derived from the **Australian Constitution**.

• This dual exchange rate system was implemented to address the **foreign exchange shortage** India faced in the early 1990s.
 
• The system aimed to **increase foreign exchange inflows**, reduce the **balance of payments crisis**, and bring more flexibility to the exchange rate policy.
 
• LERMS was a transitional measure that eventually led to the full **convertibility of the Indian rupee** on the current account.
 
• It marked a significant step in India's shift toward a **market-oriented economy** and liberalisation of its trade and financial systems.

• It created a more **competitive environment** for Indian exporters as they could access market-determined exchange rates for a portion of their earnings.
 
• The system provided a **gradual transition** toward a unified exchange rate system, which was adopted in 1993.
 
 
 
• **Background of Economic Reforms:**
 
 
• India faced a **severe balance of payments crisis** in 1991, with foreign exchange reserves barely sufficient to cover a few weeks of imports.

• The statement "**Transfer of management of public sector enterprises to private sector entrepreneurs**" correctly reflects one form of privatization. Often, governments retain ownership but allow private entities to manage operations to improve efficiency and profitability.
 
• The statement "**Non-transfer of ownership of public sector enterprises to private sector entrepreneurs**" contradicts the core concept of privatization, as privatization inherently involves some level of private sector involvement, whether in ownership or management.
 
• Privatization aims to enhance **efficiency, productivity, and competitiveness** by reducing bureaucratic control and introducing market-driven practices.
 
• Examples of privatization include the outsourcing of services, sale of public sector enterprises, or allowing private sector participation in previously government-controlled industries like telecommunications, energy, and transportation.

• **Transfer of management**__
 __

• It allows private entities to operate and manage public sector enterprises without full ownership transfer, ensuring better operational efficiency while retaining government control over strategic assets.

questions.question: Which one of the following measures of money supply is also known as 'total monetary resources of the society'?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**M3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **M3** is referred to as the measure of money supply that represents the **'total monetary resources of the society.'**
 
• It includes **M1** (currency notes and coins with the public, demand deposits with banks, and other deposits with the Reserve Bank of India) plus **time deposits** with banks.
 
• **M3** is also known as **broad money** because it provides a more comprehensive view of the money supply available in the economy.
 
• The inclusion of **time deposits** in M3 captures the savings and investment potential of the economy, making it an important indicator for policy formulation and economic analysis.
 
• **M3** is widely used in **macroeconomic analysis** to assess liquidity, inflation trends, and the overall health of the financial system.
 
• This measure is crucial for understanding the availability of money for **investment, consumption, and economic growth**.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) frequently monitors **M3** as part of its monetary policy framework to manage inflation and ensure financial stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **M1**__

 __
 
• **M1** is the most liquid measure of money supply, also known as **narrow money**.
 
• It consists of **currency notes and coins with the public**, **demand deposits** with banks, and other deposits with the RBI.
 
• Being highly liquid, **M1** is used for immediate transactions and payments.
 
 
 
• **M2**__
 __
 
• **M2** includes all components of **M1** plus **savings deposits** with post offices.
 
• This measure adds slightly less liquid assets to the highly liquid components of **M1**.
 
• **M2** is typically used for short-term economic analysis.
 
 
 
• **M4**__
 
 
• **M4** includes all components of **M3** plus **total deposits with post offices (excluding National Savings Certificates).**
 
• This is the broadest measure of money supply but is less commonly used compared to **M3**.

questions.question: Bihu festival is majorly celebrated in which of these states ?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bihu** is the most important and widely celebrated festival in the northeastern state of **Assam**.
 
• Bihu is celebrated three times a year: **Bohag Bihu** (Rongali Bihu), **Kongali Bihu** (Kati Bihu), and **Bhogali Bihu** (Magh Bihu). Each marks a different agricultural phase.
 
• **Bohag Bihu**, celebrated in April, is the Assamese New Year and the most vibrant of the three Bihus. It marks the arrival of spring and the Assamese New Year.
 
• **Kongali Bihu**, observed in October, is a solemn and austere festival focused on prayer and offerings for a good harvest.
 
• **Bhogali Bihu**, celebrated in January, signifies the end of the harvest season and is marked with feasts, bonfires, and community celebrations.
 
• During the Bihu celebrations, traditional songs and dances called **Bihu Geet** are performed, reflecting the culture and heritage of Assam.
 
• Special dishes such as **Pitha** (rice cakes) and **Laru** (sweetmeats) are prepared and enjoyed during the festivities.
 
• Bihu is a symbol of **unity** for the people of Assam, transcending religion, caste, and creed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Goa is famous for its **carnivals**, which are vibrant celebrations with parades, music, dance, and cultural performances.
 
• The state also celebrates religious festivals such as **Shigmo** and **Feast of St. Francis Xavier**.

 __
 
• The major festivals celebrated in Maharashtra include **Ganesh Chaturthi**, which is dedicated to Lord Ganesha and is observed with grandeur.
 
• Other important festivals include **Gudi Padwa**, marking the Marathi New Year, and **Diwali**.

• **Onam** is the most famous festival celebrated in Kerala, marking the harvest season and the homecoming of King Mahabali.
